svg.font-family: Outfit, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How a credential reaches one attempt
svg.desc: On the host: resolve each credential from its source; presign the run's S3 links when the pool has storage; make a random redaction key; assemble the plaintext of the binding (run, tenant, pool, start-by and end-by), the credentials, the links and the redaction key, and check it against the pool's terms; make a random 32-byte content key and encrypt the plaintext with it as a JWE with AES-256-GCM, at most 64 KiB, the envelope; encrypt the content key to the pool's current P-256 public key with ECDH-ES and A256KW, the wrap, which names the key by its thumbprint; put both in the task, sign it with the host key and publish it to the pool's tasks topic. The host can then go offline. A receiver claims the task, makes a P-256 key pair for this attempt and writes an open request with the public half to the pool's events. The key custodian unwraps the content key with the pool's private key, opens the envelope, checks the binding against the signed task and the claim, and answers with an attempt wrap, the content key encrypted to the attempt's public key, or a refusal. The receiver unwraps the content key with the attempt's private key, which stays in its memory, opens the envelope, checks the binding again, delivers the credentials to the agent's job and redacts them from its output. Three keys are involved: the content key per task, the pool key held by the custodian, and the attempt key per claim. Kafka only ever holds ciphertext.

Content key: one per task, made by the host. Encrypts the envelope. Never travels in the clear.
Pool key: P-256, private half held by the key custodian, public half in its snapshot. Carries the content key from host to custodian.
Attempt key: P-256, one per claim, private half only in the claiming receiver's memory. Carries the content key from custodian to receiver.
The binding is inside the ciphertext and the task around it is signed, so an envelope copied into another task fails the check.
